testing_gaps: run_guard's new runtime source/config drift path and bounded revoke retry path have no direct fault case: native replay covers owner loss and guard-main crash, while contract tests do not execute run_guard. A deterministic state test should change _binding after readiness, fail revoke transiently, and verify cleanup retries without restoring launch authority.

The new native replay covers supervisor-group loss and guard-main crash with an available synthetic owner. It does not cover grant expiry while the supervisor remains alive or transient Docker/owner outages followed by recovery near the cleanup deadline; those scenarios would exercise RuntimeMaxUSec/TimeoutStopUSec and retry interactions rather than just the policy values.

The native PID1 replay faults only after RootSupervisor.start returns, while the lost-create/start-ack replay explicitly replaces start_guard/check_guard. An integrated fault during an unacknowledged Docker create/start would qualify the real PID1 guard's interaction with queued mutations, persistent cgroup freezing, and scope revocation; current receipts establish those boundaries separately.
